stories.title: Ethereum's historical exchange-outflow charts can shift as more wallets get tagged
stories.summary: Analysts say Ethereum's past outflow charts are not fixed. When researchers identify new exchange wallets, old data gets relabeled, and historical charts change retroactively. This means a chart you saw months ago may look different today, even though nothing new happened on-chain.
stories.whyItMatters: Traders and analysts often cite exchange flow data as a signal for supply and demand; if that data is retroactively revised, past conclusions drawn from it may no longer hold.
whatToWatch: Whether data providers disclose when and why historical charts get revised
questions: How often do major exchange-flow datasets get revised, and by how much?

sources.title: Ethereum’s past outflow charts can change when more exchange wallets are identified

stories.title: New Treasury rules could change how stablecoin issuers return your dollars
stories.summary: The US Treasury is reportedly working on rules that would affect how stablecoin issuers handle redemptions, the process of converting a stablecoin back into dollars. CryptoSlate reports the change could alter the mechanics issuers currently use to give holders their money back.
stories.whyItMatters: Redemption reliability is the core promise behind dollar-pegged stablecoins; any rule change here affects trust in tokens widely used for trading and payments.
whatToWatch: Formal rule text or a comment period from Treasury
Public response from major stablecoin issuers
questions: Which issuers and stablecoins would the rules cover?
What is the proposed timeline for implementation?

sources.title: New Treasury rules could change how stablecoin issuers get your dollars back

stories.title: Bitcoin's push toward $85,000 hinges on ETF demand holding up after payrolls
stories.summary: Bitcoin is attempting a recovery toward $85,000, but CryptoSlate notes the move needs confirmation that ETF investors kept buying after the latest US payrolls report. Without sustained ETF inflows, the rally's durability is in question.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows have become a key gauge of institutional demand for bitcoin, and payrolls data often triggers broader market volatility that tests whether that demand holds.
whatToWatch: Daily spot bitcoin ETF flow data in the days following the payrolls report
Whether bitcoin holds above or falls back below the $85,000 level
questions: Did ETF inflows actually continue after payrolls, or did they stall?

sources.title: Bitcoin’s $85,000 recovery awaits proof that ETF investors kept buying after payrolls

stories.title: El Salvador's $666 million bitcoin reserve survives IMF review
stories.summary: El Salvador's roughly $666 million bitcoin holdings passed an International Monetary Fund review, according to CryptoSlate. The country has held bitcoin as a national reserve asset despite earlier friction with the IMF over its crypto policy.
stories.whyItMatters: El Salvador remains the clearest test case of a sovereign holding bitcoin as reserve assets, and IMF scrutiny of that experiment is a signal for how other states and lenders might treat similar moves.
whatToWatch: Any conditions or follow-up requirements the IMF attached to the review
questions: What specific standards did the reserve need to meet to pass?

sources.title: El Salvador’s $666 million Bitcoin reserve survives IMF review

stories.title: Lido proposes a new staking route requiring over 13 times the usual entry bond
stories.summary: Lido, the liquid-staking protocol, has proposed a new staking route that would require operators to post more than 13 times the bond currently needed for its default option, per CryptoSlate. The change would raise the capital commitment for node operators using this path.
stories.whyItMatters: Lido is the largest liquid-staking protocol on Ethereum, so changes to its operator requirements affect decentralization and risk across a large share of staked ETH.
whatToWatch: Whether the proposal passes Lido's governance process
Operator response to the higher bond requirement
questions: Why does this route need a bond over 13 times the default, and what risk is it meant to cover?

sources.title: Lido’s proposed staking route needs over 13 times the default entry bond

stories.title: Illinois backs delay to crypto tax rule after industry pushback
stories.summary: Illinois officials have backed delaying a crypto tax rule following months of pushback from the industry, CryptoSlate reports. The delay follows sustained lobbying and objections from crypto businesses operating in the state.
stories.whyItMatters: State-level tax treatment of crypto transactions directly affects compliance costs for exchanges and users, and a delay suggests industry pushback can still shift state policy timelines.
whatToWatch: A new effective date or revised rule text from Illinois regulators
questions: What specifically in the rule drew the strongest industry objections?

sources.title: Illinois backs delay to crypto tax rule after months of industry pushback

stories.title: Bitcoin Core fix closes a gap that could redirect funds without stealing keys
stories.summary: A new Bitcoin Core update fixes an issue that could have let funds get redirected without an attacker ever stealing private keys, according to CryptoSlate. The report does not specify the exact technical mechanism beyond this description.
stories.whyItMatters: A flaw that redirects funds without key theft is unusual and worth attention, since standard security advice around protecting private keys would not have fully covered it.
whatToWatch: Wider rollout and adoption of the patched Bitcoin Core version
Technical write-ups detailing exactly how the gap could have been exploited
questions: Was this gap ever exploited in practice, or was it found and fixed before use?

sources.title: Bitcoin Core’s new fix closes gap that could redirect funds without stealing keys

stories.title: India's local crypto exchanges capture just 0.7% of inflows, Chainalysis finds
stories.summary: Chainalysis data cited by CryptoSlate shows India's domestic crypto exchanges receive only 0.7% of the country's crypto inflows, with the large majority going through other channels. The figure points to a heavy reliance on platforms outside India's local exchange ecosystem.
stories.whyItMatters: A low share for local exchanges suggests India's crypto tax and regulatory regime may be pushing activity offshore, which matters for both enforcement and the domestic industry's viability.
whatToWatch: Any Indian regulatory response aimed at the offshore-inflow pattern
questions: Where is the remaining inflow volume actually going, and why?

sources.title: India’s local crypto exchanges get just 0.7% of inflows, Chainalysis reports

stories.title: Drift hack recovery plan opens with offer near one cent on the dollar
stories.summary: The recovery process following the Drift protocol hack has opened with an offer of roughly one cent per dollar lost, CryptoSlate reports. That is a steep discount for affected users relative to their original losses.
stories.whyItMatters: Low initial recovery offers after DeFi hacks are a recurring pattern and shape how much trust users place in a protocol's post-incident handling.
whatToWatch: Whether the recovery offer improves through negotiation or further funds recovery
Drift's official statement on total losses and next steps
questions: How was the one-cent recovery figure calculated, and could it rise?

sources.title: Drift hack recovery opened near one cent per dollar lost

stories.title: Vitalik-inspired AI payment system can send expired deposits to its own treasury
stories.summary: A new AI payment system reportedly inspired by Vitalik Buterin includes a feature where expired deposits get sent to the system's treasury rather than returned, per CryptoSlate. The report does not detail the full mechanics of how or why deposits expire.
stories.whyItMatters: Any system that can route user funds to its own treasury by default, rather than back to the user, raises questions worth watching as AI-linked payment tools expand in crypto.
whatToWatch: Documentation clarifying when and why deposits expire
Community or developer reaction to the treasury-routing design
questions: Under what conditions does a deposit count as expired?
Can users reclaim funds before expiry, and how is that communicated?

sources.title: Vitalik-inspired AI payment system can send expired deposits to its treasury
